title: Tech Note: Connecting to a 4D Server
author: Christian Cypert
featured_technology: OP Count network components / OP Get network component info
OP Select 4D Server / OP Find 4D Server
OP Close connection / OP Delete 4D Server / OP Unload network component

historical_commentary.text: The 4D Open plug-in and its OP-prefixed connection API were the standard, and at the time only, way to programmatically connect a client application to a specific 4D Server outside of 4D's normal interactive connection dialog. This entire mechanism is now obsolete: current 4D applications rely on the built-in remote/client-server architecture for interactive sessions, and on ORDA remote datastores (introduced in 4D v17+) for programmatic cross-database access, neither of which requires a separate connectivity plug-in or the manual network-component enumeration shown here.
related_updates: 4D's native client-server architecture and ORDA remote datastores have superseded the 4D Open plug-in for connecting to remote 4D Servers
Programmatic cross-database access today is done via ORDA remote datastores rather than the OP Open connection-based API described in this note
